matching service imagery to a relevant observable feature
distinguishing the subject from a broad keyword or venue association
keeping selection separate from cropping, layout and evidential claims
prerequisites: An intended message, audience and defined job for the image.
Known source provenance and the ability to inspect images in the final frame.
not_ideal_when: Mood, metaphor or aspiration is the actual communication purpose and a literal view would narrow it unnecessarily.
The source is being treated as proof of facts it cannot establish.
A diagram, procedure or no image would serve the task better.
example_user_queries: This photograph looks beautiful but does not explain what we offer.
My workshop picture shows finished objects instead of what participants will do.
Does this image show the feature people are booking?
Our room page uses a shared-office photograph.
I matched the word library but the article is about sharing seeds.
How do I choose between an atmospheric photo and an informative one?
Could this picture imply something the copy does not support?
Can a generated illustration prove what a real venue looks like?
Should I choose another source or just crop this one?
What should the picture add when the words already explain the basics?

related_patterns.relationship: Establishes the intended message; image selection chooses a relevant visible contribution.
Identifies which associations, knowledge and expectations the intended audience can bring.
Adjusts framing within a chosen source; image selection decides which source contributes the intended meaning.
Coordinates source imagery with words through complementary meaning, placement and explicit visual reference.

visual_decision.reason: Three photographic selection-only comparisons change one selected-photo href each: finished ceramic to handbuilding activity, shared workspace to enclosed room, book library to seed-packing materials. Both full 3:2 sources use the same fixed frame; all native typography, copy, layout, colors, paper and presentation stay fixed.

sources.supports: Contextual guidance to choose relevant, clear images that support content rather than occupy space.
Government service guidance favors lifelike photography for relevant representation and discourages generic stock atmosphere; not a universal rule for campaigns.
Documentary accuracy guidance emphasizes honest photographic context and accurate captions.
An informative image’s text alternative conveys relevant meaning, and its role depends on the reason for including it.

patterns.title: Crop for Impact
patterns.short_description: Adjust the visible window within an image to emphasize useful content, protect important outlines and retain necessary context, while keeping the framing truthful to its purpose.
use_when: The entire source gives supporting surroundings more space than the intended action needs.
A fixed crop clips a product feature that exists in the source.
A close crop omits the context needed to understand an offer.
goals: Choose a retained source region according to the communication task.
Distinguish tightening, equal-scale shifting and widening.
Preserve important outlines, context and truthful representation.
mechanisms: fitting a smaller source window enlarges retained content inside a fixed frame
shifting an equal-size window exchanges peripheral content without zoom
widening can restore a relationship or feature
crop boundaries determine which meaningful outlines survive
aspect-ratio matching preserves geometry while output requirements limit useful magnification
prerequisites: The uncropped source and a clear communication purpose.
Known final frame proportions and ability to inspect output size.
not_ideal_when: The source never contained the needed feature.
The crop removes context that changes the apparent meaning or truth of an image.
Too few retained pixels remain for the intended output.
example_user_queries: The subject gets lost when I fit the whole photo into this invitation.
Can I tighten the view without changing the page layout?
My square product picture cuts through the handle.
Could I move the crop instead of zooming out?
The image looks cleaner but no longer shows the room is enclosed.
When does a wider crop communicate more clearly?
This crop works in a banner but clips details in a square tile.
How do I keep a photo from stretching when I fit it?
What important context am I removing at the edges?
The source is too small after a tight crop.

related_patterns.relationship: Selects the source; cropping adjusts which part of that source remains visible.
Changes relative element sizes in the layout; fitting a crop can change apparent scale inside a fixed frame.
Treats the supporting layer behind important content, including interference that remains inside a retained crop.
Coordinates source imagery with words through complementary meaning, placement and explicit visual reference.

visual_decision.reason: Three crop-only photographic comparisons tighten an action, shift an equal-size square and widen to restore context. One image-window viewBox changes in each fixed artifact; source bytes, type, copy, colors and presentation remain identical. Exact source-view insets explain the retained regions with dashed-before and solid-after boundaries.

sources.supports: Distinguishes cropping retained content from resizing; preserving aspect ratio avoids distortion and output size affects image quality.
Image fitting can clip to fill an element box while preserving aspect ratio; delivered container proportions matter.
Visual-journalism guidance emphasizes accurate captions and honest context; composition does not justify misleading omission.

patterns.title: Control the Background
patterns.short_description: Adjust the detail, tone or opacity of the layer behind important content so it supports the communication without hiding necessary context.
use_when: Photographic edges interfere with lettering despite useful subject matter.
Decorative texture competes with a product contour or handle opening.
A translucent information card transmits changing image detail.
goals: Target the supporting layer rather than unnecessarily changing foreground content.
Choose between local protection, pattern attenuation and an opaque information surface.
Preserve useful photographic context and acknowledge what treatment conceals.
mechanisms: local opaque backing removes photographic variation immediately behind text
lower pattern opacity reduces decorative edge contrast while preserving geometry
opaque surfaces decouple the effective ground from underlying image content
treatment extent determines which context stays visible
foreground contrast must be checked against the delivered local background
prerequisites: A defined foreground communication task.
Access to the background layer or a source image suited to the layout.
not_ideal_when: Surrounding detail supplies evidence or context needed to understand the subject.
The source image contributes the wrong meaning.
Many local patches are compensating for an unsuitable overall layout.
example_user_queries: The date gets lost against the furniture in my photograph.
Can I keep the image without making the lettering larger?
The product outline is clear but the brand pattern feels too busy.
The pattern through the handle distracts from the object.
My translucent card shows photo details through the price.
How can I protect the facts without fading the whole page?
Will blurring the image actually improve the text contrast?
A different responsive crop puts a bright patch behind my title.
How much of the image should a text backing cover?
The cleaner background hides context the reader needs.

related_patterns.relationship: Describes foreground/background perception; controlling the supporting layer is one intervention that can strengthen separation.
Adjusts light-dark differences; background control also addresses detail, transparency and treatment extent.
Changes the visible source window; background treatments address interference remaining inside it.
Selects the source for its contribution; a quiet backdrop cannot make irrelevant imagery meaningful.

visual_decision.reason: Three background-only opacity changes: add a local opaque text backing, attenuate decorative waves behind an identical product cutout, and make a booking information surface opaque. Existing generated assets and all foreground typography/copy/geometry/crops/presentation remain fixed.

sources.supports: Image features can interfere with foreground letter shapes; check local image contrast behind letters.
Rosenholtz, Li and Nakano (2007) investigate visual clutter measures and their relationship to search performance in complex imagery; not a test of these designs.
Treating the area immediately behind text can maintain sufficient local text/background contrast.
Minimum text contrast thresholds and defined exceptions; a limited color-pair check does not establish complete conformance.

patterns.title: Integrate Text and Image
patterns.short_description: Coordinate the meaning, placement and connections of words and pictures so viewers can understand what belongs together while each remains useful and readable.
use_when: Relevant pictures and offer details are separated by unrelated material.
Feature names need an explicit connection to locations in an image.
Readable lettering covers the part of a photograph that contributes necessary meaning.
goals: Coordinate complementary information across words and pictures.
Make caption and label referents clear.
Preserve both image content and text readability at delivered sizes.
mechanisms: adjacent offers reduce the distance between a photograph and corresponding practical details
leader endpoints disambiguate exact feature locations
coordinated text placement preserves the visual contribution of a subject
wording identifies what the image alone cannot establish
responsive grouping and text alternatives preserve relationships across delivery modes
prerequisites: Relevant imagery and an identified communication purpose.
Access to layout and native typography.
not_ideal_when: The selected source is irrelevant or implies the wrong relationship.
The brief intentionally separates image experience from reference details.
Labels require more detail than the image can show at the intended size.
example_user_queries: The pictures are relevant but their captions feel disconnected.
Readers have to look back and forth to match each offer with its image.
Can I move the offer details closer without redesigning the page?
My feature names do not show which part of the product they mean.
Should I use a leader line or just put the label nearby?
The headline is readable but hides the face in the portrait.
How do I give words and pictures different useful jobs?
Do I have to overlay lettering to make a page feel integrated?
On mobile all the images come before all the captions.
The caption repeats the picture without helping explain it.

related_patterns.relationship: Chooses which source contributes useful meaning; integration coordinates that source with words.
Supplies one grouping mechanism; integration additionally addresses exact visual reference, complementary meaning and interference.
Protects foreground readability; legible text can still conceal necessary image content.
Changes the retained source window; integration can also be achieved with fixed crops and frames.

visual_decision.reason: Three controlled relationships: move offer blocks beside fixed photographs, reveal feature leaders over a fixed product cutout, and move an unchanged title panel off a portrait face. Exact photograph bytes/crops, words, font settings and unrelated geometry/presentation stay identical.

sources.supports: Moreno and Mayer (1999), Cognitive Principles of Multimedia Learning: The Role of Modality and Contiguity, found a spatial-contiguity effect for words near vs far from an instructional animation. Specific educational evidence, not a test of these artifacts.
Foreground lettering needs adequate local contrast against its actual background, including photographic variation.
Text alternatives for complex visual information should preserve essential information and relationships; adjacency is insufficient alone.

patterns.title: Simplify Through Abstraction
patterns.short_description: Replace incidental appearance with selected shapes, relationships or steps that preserve the information needed for a particular recognition or understanding task.
use_when: A category cue is tied to the material appearance of one specimen.
Perspective and decor obscure a conceptual arrangement summary.
A photograph shows materials but not the relationships in a written procedure.
goals: Select the features or relationships required by the communication task.
Change representation without inventing precision or unsupported information.
Explain what is lost and when the detailed source remains preferable.
mechanisms: defining feature combinations preserve category recognition while surface appearance is omitted
a conceptual overhead model replaces perspective with selected spatial relationships
schematic symbols and arrows encode a known procedure
labels and external text make the intended model explicit
purpose determines which details can be omitted and which must survive
prerequisites: A defined recognition or understanding task.
A trustworthy brief specifying relationships that must survive.
not_ideal_when: Readers must inspect real materials, exact dimensions, state or evidence.
Simplification deletes the feature that distinguishes the subject.
Clean geometry would imply unsupported precision.
example_user_queries: The category picture looks like one specific product instead of a general cue.
Which features should I keep when turning a photo into a drawing?
The room photograph shows atmosphere but makes the arrangement hard to summarize.
Can I show the layout without pretending to have measured it?
The materials photo does not explain the task order.
How do I turn written steps into a simple visual model?
My simplified icon has lost the part that makes it recognizable.
Does fewer detail always mean clearer communication?
The diagram looks authoritative but the dimensions are only approximate.
When should I keep a photograph instead of simplifying it?

related_patterns.relationship: Removes unnecessary content; abstraction also changes how remaining information is represented.
Establishes the contribution an image must make and therefore which features an abstraction should preserve.
Connects labels and explanations with visual models, making their intended reading explicit.
Uses solid tone to prioritize a fixed figure contour and openings rather than broader representational changes.

visual_decision.reason: Three photographic-to-native representation changes preserve selected defining features, a conceptual spatial arrangement and a written task sequence. Only the clipped image-frame contents change; all external text, fonts, dimensions, surroundings and presentation remain fixed. Original drawings are intentionally schematic and not exact traces or measured plans.

sources.supports: IBM guidance calls for essential purposeful elements and distinguishes icon/pictogram uses; not universal experimental evidence.

Larkin and Simon (1987) theoretically analyze diagrammatic and verbal representations in illustrative problems; search, explicit information and inference depend on representation. Does not test these photo transformations.
Purpose-directed cartographic selection and simplification should retain characteristic features and important relationships.
Complex diagrams need text equivalents conveying essential information and relationships; fewer details alone do not establish accessibility.

patterns.title: Use Silhouettes
patterns.short_description: Use a solid-toned figure to emphasize a subject’s contour and meaningful openings when those shapes can carry the message without internal detail.
use_when: Surface finish is irrelevant to a category cue but dominates its photograph.
A silhouette has useful contour and gaps but weak separation from its ground.
A flat figure needs review because the brief requires interior detail.
goals: Use contour and negative spaces deliberately when they carry the message.
Preserve the same source geometry while removing internal RGB information.
Recognize when another representation is more appropriate.
mechanisms: constant-tone interiors suppress material and lighting cues while retaining source alpha
transparent openings retain meaningful shape structure
background contrast makes outside and inside boundaries more distinct
viewpoint affects which parts remain distinguishable after detail removal
restoring internal detail repairs briefs that exceed silhouette information
prerequisites: A defined image contribution and a suitable source view.
A clean figure boundary and meaningful transparent gaps.
not_ideal_when: The brief requires facial features, material condition or mechanisms.
The selected view merges important parts.
Similar objects differ mainly inside the boundary.
example_user_queries: The category sign looks like it accepts only one product finish.
Can this object still be recognized without shading?
The handle disappears when I fill the shape.
The gap between the blades is hard to see on the dark background.
Should I change the silhouette or the surface behind it?
My silhouette looks clean but the object is ambiguous.
The head-on view merges all the important parts.
The speaker poster loses the face when I flatten it.
When should I restore a photograph instead of using a solid shape?
How do I keep the outline exactly the same while removing surface detail?

related_patterns.relationship: Broader reduction can preserve internal lines, change viewpoint or encode processes; silhouettes prioritize filled contour and openings.
Establishes perceptual subject/background distinction on which a silhouette strongly depends.
Repairs silhouette separation by treating its supporting layer without changing shape.
Determines whether the image needs internal detail or can contribute through shape alone.

visual_decision.reason: Three controlled decisions: flatten an unchanged pitcher cutout while preserving its handle opening; change only the ground behind a fixed open-shears silhouette; restore photographic detail to the same maker cutout when the portrait brief requires it. Native alpha-preserving filters, fixed frames/type/copy/presentation and exact source bytes isolate the interventions.

sources.supports: Wagemans et al. (2008) found substantial variation in identifiability of silhouette/outline object versions; recognizability should not be assumed.
Mitsumatsu and Yokosawa (2002) investigate internal detail and foreshortening; useful orientation information can be lost in silhouettes.
Contrast requirements for meaningful web graphical information against adjacent colors, with defined scope and exceptions.

patterns.title: Use Visual Metaphors
patterns.short_description: Borrow a recognizable quality or relationship from one subject to communicate another, making the intended comparison clear and checking the implications it brings with it.
use_when: Literal topic imagery does not show the relationship the campaign wants to propose.
A coherent metaphor image leaves the intended subject ambiguous.
An attractive comparison imports implications that conflict with the brief.
goals: Specify the subject, borrowed source and intended transferred relationship.
Use visual conjunction or explanatory wording to make the comparison interpretable.
Review unwanted properties and alternatives before committing to a metaphor.
mechanisms: conjoining a book and seedling visually proposes a growth relationship
explicit wording identifies a target for an unchanged visual source
source selection changes which relational structure is available to transfer
audience knowledge and message familiarity influence interpretation
keeping practical facts explicit limits dependence on metaphor decoding
prerequisites: A clear communication claim and intended audience.
Ability to describe the proposed comparison in plain language.
not_ideal_when: The brief needs literal evidence, measured diagrams or precise instructions.
Shared background knowledge cannot be assumed for a necessary message.
The image suggests unsupported performance or inevitable outcomes.
example_user_queries: My picture is attractive but nobody knows what it is explaining.
How can I show what reading contributes rather than just show a book?
The tangled thread looks like a sewing class instead of a planning session.
Could one clear sentence anchor the image without replacing it?
The ladder image implies ranked levels but this event is about exchange.
Which unintended qualities might people transfer from this image?
The comparison is clever but does not support the actual claim.
Do viewers need cultural knowledge to understand this visual?
When should I use a literal photograph instead of a metaphor?
How do I tell whether I am showing a metaphor or a familiar symbol?

related_patterns.relationship: Determines an image’s contribution; metaphor differs from literal topic illustration or documentation.
Coordinates image with words that can name the target and anchor the transferred relationship.
Can realize a metaphor through letterforms but can also operate without cross-domain comparison.
Draws on established associations rather than asking the audience to construct a fresh cross-domain comparison.

visual_decision.reason: Three photographic comparisons introduce a seedling over a fixed book, change one anchoring sentence beside an unchanged cord image, and replace a ladder with a bridge. Native typography/layout isolate the intended cues. The third pair explicitly changes source-object geometry and photographic appearance as part of metaphor selection.

sources.supports: Forceville (2017), Visual and Multimodal Metaphor in Advertising: Cultural Perspectives, discusses source/target/feature interpretation and dependence on cultural knowledge.
Gentner (1983) supplies a theoretical account of selective relational mapping across domains; no universal design performance claim.
Petridis and Chilton (2019) document interpretation errors and a correlation between message familiarity and interpretation in studied visual metaphors; not a test of these designs.

patterns.title: Employ Recognizable Symbols
patterns.short_description: Use visual signs whose meanings the intended audience can already recognize, match them to the actual service or action, and add words where the meaning remains uncertain.
use_when: A brand ornament is being asked to identify a practical service.
A familiar icon contradicts the action or label it accompanies.
People recognize an object but cannot infer the service behind it.
goals: Select a convention suited to the actual audience and medium.
Keep the selected symbol semantically consistent with its service or action.
Retain visible words for meanings the symbol cannot communicate precisely.
mechanisms: learned associations offer a candidate meaning before all wording is read
agreement among symbol, label and context supports one interpretation
visible wording disambiguates services represented by the same familiar object
recognizability and interpretation require separate evaluation
prerequisites: A defined audience, service or action and intended medium.
Access to conventions used in that audience’s context.
not_ideal_when: A symbol would require as much explanation as the complete text label.
The brief needs a novel conceptual comparison rather than an established cue.
A precise service or specification cannot be represented by the familiar sign alone.
example_user_queries: The symbols fit our brand but visitors cannot tell which service they mark.
People can identify the headphones but do not know what we offer.
Is my upload-looking arrow wrong for a download button?
Can I make the information icon match our identity without losing its meaning?
Would a plain text button be clearer than this pictogram?
Our icon works for regular users but newcomers keep guessing.
How do I check what people expect a symbol to do?
Do I still need a label beside a familiar icon?
We use the same mark for help, events and featured content.
How do I avoid assuming everybody shares our visual conventions?

related_patterns.relationship: Chooses defining visual detail; an abstracted shape still needs a recognizable meaning.
Proposes a comparison; recognizable symbols draw on existing learned associations.
Names the precise service or outcome when a familiar shape leaves interpretation uncertain.
Adds independent cues; a symbol must be understood to carry redundant meaning.

visual_decision.reason: Three controlled photo-led designs replace a brand rosette with a circled i, change upload to download while preserving the tray/button, and reveal an Audio guide label beside unchanged headphones. Only native symbol href or label opacity changes.

sources.supports: Nielsen Norman Group distinguishes recognizability from interpretation and reports user-research examples of ambiguous object recognition and function prediction.
W3C cognitive accessibility note recommends clear familiar symbols, attention to culture and text support. Supplemental guidance, not an independent WCAG conformance test.
GC Design System documents action and state associations including downloading a file.
USWDS documents accessible icon naming and handling accompanying text links without duplicate announcements.
Nielsen Norman Group identifies experience-dependent icon interpretation and recommends visible text labels to reduce ambiguity.

graphics.title: Define the Core Message
graphics.mechanism: Decide what this audience should take away from this piece before choosing how to emphasize it.
graphics.reading: One statement is selected from several possible ideas and connected to a single accented message block, making the intended takeaway explicit.

graphics.title: Use Scale to Establish Importance
graphics.mechanism: Make relative sizes express what the viewer needs first, while keeping supporting information readable.
graphics.reading: Three related squares share a baseline; the large accented square leads, while medium ink and small gray squares remain visible as supporting levels.

graphics.title: Design for the Audience
graphics.mechanism: Adapt language, information priority, and presentation to people's knowledge, tasks, and viewing conditions.
graphics.reading: Three different constraint profiles connect to corresponding adjusted message forms. Green marks the matched forms; each preserves a different arrangement rather than assuming one treatment fits every situation.

graphics.title: Match Form to Purpose
graphics.mechanism: Choose a structure and format that let people use the information for the task the design must support.
graphics.reading: One content block branches toward an ordered stack, aligned grid and segmented strip. Green marks different usable structures selected according to the task, rather than a single format imposed on every encounter.

graphics.title: Remove the Nonessential
graphics.mechanism: Remove elements that do not earn their place in this encounter while preserving meaning, identity, and necessary conditions.
graphics.reading: Three content-bearing bars survive at their original levels while interleaved gray marks disappear. Green identifies retained material, emphasizing selective removal rather than stripping everything away.

graphics.title: Make Meaning Explicit
graphics.mechanism: State the relationship, scope, or consequence that a viewer would otherwise have to infer from an ambiguous design.
graphics.reading: Two different forms connect directly to their own explanation blocks. Green marks the explanations that make each mapping explicit, instead of leaving the meaning of the visible forms to inference.

graphics.title: Chunk Information
graphics.mechanism: Organize material into useful units so readers can locate a part, understand what belongs together, and handle detail without reconstructing the structure.
graphics.reading: The same six bars remain on both sides. On the right, wider gaps and green brackets express three paired content units. Grouping changes relationships without deleting detail; three pairs illustrate this case rather than prescribing a universal group count.

graphics.title: Sequence the Message
graphics.mechanism: Arrange content so readers encounter context, dependencies, and supporting detail in an order suited to what they need to understand or do.
graphics.reading: A triangle, square and circle remain intact while their vertical order changes. The green connector follows the reordered column from top to bottom. The different forms represent content units, not a prescribed universal sequence.

graphics.title: Establish a Focal Point
graphics.mechanism: Give a meaningful element or group a distinct leading role so the composition offers a useful place to begin.
graphics.reading: Six equally sized circles form a field. Five retain quiet open outlines; one receives a green filled treatment. The leading role comes from selective treatment relative to its neighbors, without changing the size of any circle.

graphics.title: Create Deliberate Contrast
graphics.mechanism: Use a visible difference in a chosen attribute to clarify a meaningful distinction, while keeping unrelated elements consistent.
graphics.reading: Two paths share the same span and stroke width. One is continuous and the other segmented. The green path represents an alternative identity treatment without making either path larger or prescribing a dominant anchor.

graphics.title: Differentiate Levels of Importance
graphics.mechanism: Assign content to meaningful levels and give each role a consistent visual treatment, while keeping necessary detail accessible.
graphics.reading: Each row repeats the same treatment across two elements. A heavy green pair leads, a medium ink pair supports, and a thin ink pair provides a quieter level. Consistency within roles matters as well as distinction between them; three levels illustrate a case, not a universal rule.

graphics.title: Establish a Clear Reading Order
graphics.mechanism: Make the intended route through content apparent through sequence cues, continuity, and layouts that preserve meaningful order across presentations.
graphics.reading: Four equal units remain peers while a green path identifies one continuous row-by-row route. Connectors and arrowheads express succession rather than relative size or rank. This is one illustrated route, not a universal reading pattern.

graphics.title: Guide the Eye
graphics.mechanism: Orient visual cues toward useful destinations so attention has a coherent invitation to continue.
graphics.reading: A curved green arrow leaves a solid starting point and ends above an outlined destination. It illustrates a meaningful directional connection, not an observed fixation trace or a compulsory reading sequence.

graphics.title: Align to Common Edges
graphics.mechanism: Give related elements shared reference edges so their placement expresses a clear and dependable relationship.
graphics.reading: Three equal-height blocks of different lengths start on the same green reference edge. Their shared origin expresses alignment without implying a complete grid or a hierarchy of sizes.

graphics.title: Establish a Grid
graphics.mechanism: Define reusable margins, tracks, gutters, and spans so layout decisions form a coherent system that can adapt to content and format.
graphics.reading: Four narrow green tracks form one framework. A dark full-width region and two lower two-track regions show different allowed spans. The mark expresses reusable layout relationships, not a requirement that all content occupy identical cells.

graphics.title: Balance Visual Weight
graphics.mechanism: Distribute visual weight across a composition so its parts form an intentional whole while preserving meaningful emphasis.
graphics.reading: A larger open region and a smaller solid region sit on opposite sides of a shared field. Their unequal size and treatment illustrate asymmetric counterpoint, not calibrated visual weights or a rule that a particular pair is numerically balanced.

graphics.title: Use Negative Space
graphics.mechanism: Allocate open areas around, between and within elements to clarify relationships and give important content room without weakening necessary connections.
graphics.reading: An open boundary surrounds a compact content group with a generous, visible buffer. The gap is purposeful room rather than missing content.

graphics.title: Establish Consistent Spacing
graphics.mechanism: Assign repeatable spacing rules to equivalent relationships so gaps and insets communicate structure reliably while allowing content to vary.
graphics.reading: Three equal blocks repeat with equal intervals. Two matching accent markers identify the gaps, showing a repeated spatial relationship rather than a universal spacing value.

graphics.title: Use Proportional Relationships
graphics.mechanism: Relate selected dimensions through explicit ratios or multipliers so space and size follow content needs and remain coordinated when a reference value changes.
graphics.reading: Two panels of equal height have widths in a two-to-one relationship, separated by a fixed gap. The mark shows an explicit allocation, not a claim of universal beauty or perceptual balance.

graphics.title: Establish Visual Rhythm
graphics.mechanism: Coordinate recurring elements and intervals through deliberate repetition, variation and pauses so the composition's pace supports its content.
graphics.reading: Two matching primary-accent pairs recur with a larger interval between them. Repetition, variation and a pause form one readable sequence; no fixed viewing tempo is implied.

graphics.title: Frame the Content
graphics.mechanism: Define a purposeful field or boundary around content so its scope and relation to its surroundings are clear, using only the enclosure the task needs.
graphics.reading: Four corner brackets define a field around three content marks with visible inner clearance. The boundary serves the content rather than enclosing each mark individually.

graphics.title: Break the Grid Deliberately
graphics.mechanism: Make a purposeful exception to a stated grid rule while keeping the surrounding structure and essential reading relationships dependable.
graphics.reading: A single accent module crosses track references while the surrounding grid stays visible. The exception is defined by the retained structure rather than by arbitrary displacement alone.

graphics.title: Group Related Elements Through Proximity
graphics.mechanism: Place elements that belong together closer to one another than to competing neighbors so distance reinforces the intended relationship.
graphics.reading: Each pair has a small internal gap; a larger central interval separates the two groups. Matching marks occur in both pairs, so proximity supplies local membership while shared appearance connects their roles.

graphics.title: Signal Relationships Through Similarity
graphics.mechanism: Give elements that share a meaningful category or role a recognizable visual feature, and avoid sharing that feature where it would imply a false relationship.
graphics.reading: Circles and squares repeat their shared appearance across separated positions. Similarity identifies two feature categories within the same array rather than relying on a single local cluster.

graphics.title: Establish Visual Continuity
graphics.mechanism: Make the position and direction of separated marks support the intended continuation of a path or contour, while preserving meaningful breaks.
graphics.reading: Two visible segments occupy one extended diagonal while a filled panel interrupts the middle. Position and direction support a common continuation through the interruption.

graphics.title: Separate Figure from Ground
graphics.mechanism: Give the content that must read as a distinct object or layer a dependable boundary against its surroundings, using a ground that supports that distinction.
graphics.reading: A compact accent disc has a distinct closed contour against a larger unbroken ink field. The field remains visible around the figure, making their roles distinguishable without adding a shadow.

graphics.title: Use Implied Forms
graphics.mechanism: Leave parts of a visual form undrawn or hidden while retaining enough contour and identifying features for the intended whole to remain recognizable.
graphics.reading: Four retained corners support the interpretation of one square even though the middle edge sections are absent. The accent highlights one contributing fragment rather than a second shape.

graphics.title: Group Elements Within Shared Boundaries
graphics.mechanism: Enclose elements that belong to the same meaningful unit, keeping unrelated elements outside so the visible region expresses the intended membership.
graphics.reading: A single shared outline contains three different marks, while a matching mark outside the region remains separate. Enclosure, rather than visual similarity alone, expresses intended membership.

graphics.title: Match Typeface to Context
graphics.mechanism: Choose a typeface and its appropriate cut for the reader’s task, intended voice, required characters, and actual viewing and production conditions.
graphics.reading: A serifed display letter and a clearly differentiated upright character show that letterforms can be selected for different communication tasks. The accent emphasizes the diagnostic character rather than a universal preferred type category.

graphics.title: Pair Complementary Typefaces
graphics.mechanism: Give selected typefaces distinct, compatible roles and apply those roles consistently so the combination supports one communication purpose.
graphics.reading: A serifed letter and a sans serif letter share a baseline and comparable extent while keeping distinct forms. The mark represents coordinated roles rather than identical shapes or a universally preferred pair.

graphics.title: Establish a Type Scale
graphics.mechanism: Choose a limited set of type sizes, assign them to recurring text roles, and adapt the relationships to the medium while preserving readable supporting text.
graphics.reading: Three T forms share a baseline while increasing in size, representing a selected vocabulary of reusable text sizes rather than arbitrary local variations or a prescribed numerical ratio.

graphics.title: Control Line Length
graphics.mechanism: Set the width available to prose so lines support the reading task, allowing natural reflow while preserving readable type and accommodating the surrounding layout.
graphics.reading: An accent dimension shows a chosen horizontal measure above bracketed text lines. The line endings vary naturally within the chosen width rather than filling the page or forcing identical lengths.

graphics.title: Adjust Line Spacing
graphics.mechanism: Set the interval between lines to support the reading task, separating lines enough to follow while keeping connected text cohesive.
graphics.reading: Three equal text lines retain their horizontal shape while a vertical dimension marks the interval between baselines. The accent concerns line separation rather than changing letter size.

graphics.title: Apply Optical Alignment
graphics.mechanism: Make small, shape-aware positioning adjustments when numerical alignment leaves visible text edges or centers looking uneven.
graphics.reading: Three text-like rows share a visible edge while a small accent opening mark hangs outside it. The left rule remains a reference; only the mark crosses it.

graphics.title: Adjust Letter Spacing
graphics.mechanism: Adjust spacing across a text run or between a particular pair to suit its letterforms, size and role while preserving coherent words and necessary word boundaries.
graphics.reading: Two letter-like stem forms keep their size while a short accent dimension occupies their internal interval. The adjustment concerns separation within a run, not moving the entire line.

graphics.title: Control Line Breaks
graphics.mechanism: Choose where text continues onto a new line so phrasing, meaningful expressions and paragraph endings support the reading task without sacrificing adaptable layout.
graphics.reading: Text-like rows retain a shared starting edge while a bent accent arrow indicates a deliberate continuation onto a new line. The intervention changes the boundary rather than the letter size or line interval.

graphics.title: Use Type as Image
graphics.mechanism: Make letterforms, their arrangement or their interior spaces carry a relevant visual idea while preserving an appropriate route to reading the message.
graphics.reading: A recognizable U retains its open top and curved base while a small handle lets the same letter also suggest a vessel.

graphics.title: Limit the Palette
graphics.mechanism: Consolidate colors that do not carry distinct useful meanings, retaining the colors needed for identity, differentiation, state and readable contrast.
graphics.reading: A compact palette card repeats a dark swatch and retains one contrasting accent, suggesting deliberate reuse rather than a unique color for each item. The number of pictured swatches is illustrative, not a universal limit.

graphics.title: Assign Consistent Color Roles
graphics.mechanism: Define what colors signify within a design system or document, then preserve those assignments across equivalent actions, categories and states.
graphics.reading: One accent source branches to two applications with the same accent fill, expressing a stable assignment reused in multiple places.

graphics.title: Use Complementary Contrast
graphics.mechanism: Use opposing hue families to create a purposeful distinction, then adjust their lightness, saturation and distribution for the actual communication task.
graphics.reading: Two different markers occupy opposite ends of a circle’s diameter, indicating an opposing relationship on a specified hue wheel. The mark uses the library palette rather than reproducing a literal color wheel.

graphics.title: Build Analogous Harmony
graphics.mechanism: Choose neighboring hue families to give related material a shared color character, while preserving the variation and tonal separation its purpose requires.
graphics.reading: Three markers occupy neighboring positions along one side of a circle, indicating a local hue neighborhood. The mark uses the library palette; its marker count is illustrative rather than a required palette size.

graphics.title: Establish Value Contrast
graphics.mechanism: Adjust light-dark relationships so necessary text, boundaries and priorities separate from their surroundings, without giving every element maximum contrast.
graphics.reading: A filled region and open outlined region share a central edge. The mark represents visible separation between tonal fields in the library palette rather than a measured color specimen.

graphics.title: Test in Grayscale
graphics.mechanism: Temporarily remove hue and saturation to inspect which text, distinctions and action cues survive, then repair the original design and review both versions again.
graphics.reading: Filled and outlined specimens sit beside an accent inspection lens. This library-palette concept mark represents examination, not a simulated grayscale color specimen.

graphics.title: Reinforce Meaning Beyond Color
graphics.mechanism: Give color-coded information another visible carrier, such as words, shapes or line patterns, so the intended meaning remains available without identifying the hue.
graphics.reading: A circle and triangle differ in form as well as library color. The two identities remain distinguishable from their outlines when hue is unavailable; the article supplies meaningful labels and mappings.

graphics.title: Choose Images for Meaning
graphics.mechanism: Select imagery for the specific activity, feature, subject or association the viewer needs to understand, and check that its visible content supports the surrounding message without implying unsupported facts.
graphics.reading: A framed image carries a small accent check. The mark represents selecting visual content for a defined communication job rather than changing its size or frame.

graphics.title: Crop for Impact
graphics.mechanism: Adjust the visible window within an image to emphasize useful content, protect important outlines and retain necessary context, while keeping the framing truthful to its purpose.
graphics.reading: Crossing right-angle guides define a retained rectangle. Their extensions recall a crop tool and distinguish the chosen window from the complete source.

graphics.title: Control the Background
graphics.mechanism: Adjust the detail, tone or opacity of the layer behind important content so it supports the communication without hiding necessary context.
graphics.reading: Three parallel background contours stop at a calm central surface carrying a small accent form. The supporting layer changes while the foreground stays distinct.

graphics.title: Integrate Text and Image
graphics.mechanism: Coordinate the meaning, placement and connections of words and pictures so viewers can understand what belongs together while each remains useful and readable.
graphics.reading: A framed image and two text lines form a pair. An accent elbow connects text to a point within the image, making their reference explicit.

graphics.title: Simplify Through Abstraction
graphics.mechanism: Replace incidental appearance with selected shapes, relationships or steps that preserve the information needed for a particular recognition or understanding task.
graphics.reading: An irregular outlined form with internal marks becomes a simple bounded form. The connecting accent indicates a deliberate change of representation while a central internal feature survives.

graphics.title: Use Silhouettes
graphics.mechanism: Use a solid-toned figure to emphasize a subject’s contour and meaningful openings when those shapes can carry the message without internal detail.
graphics.reading: A single filled vessel retains its lip and an open loop handle. The handle opening remains negative space, distinguishing silhouette structure from a featureless filled blob.

graphics.title: Use Visual Metaphors
graphics.mechanism: Borrow a recognizable quality or relationship from one subject to communicate another, making the intended comparison clear and checking the implications it brings with it.
graphics.reading: A sprout joins an open book: the book is treated as a growing medium, suggesting development of ideas rather than merely depicting reading material.

graphics.title: Employ Recognizable Symbols
graphics.mechanism: Use visual signs whose meanings the intended audience can already recognize, match them to the actual service or action, and add words where the meaning remains uncertain.
graphics.reading: A familiar circled i supplies an information cue while a separate accent line stands for a confirming text label. It represents using a convention with words, not universal recognition.
